claims.text: A man reported as 62 years old, of Zambian geographic origin and living in the UK since 1994, had HIV, gout and diet-controlled type 2 diabetes. His original HIV diagnosis followed constitutional symptoms; efavirenz, emtricitabine and tenofovir were initially tolerated for years. August 2018 latent-TB IGRA was positive with normal liver, blood-count and renal tests. Six months of isoniazid 300 mg with pyridoxine 10 mg were completed without adverse effects, followed by normal March 2019 chest imaging and discharge from TB care. In May 2022 he was asymptomatic with ALT 167, AST 154, GGT 147 and ALP 178 IU/L. Bilirubin, albumin and INR were normal, with unremarkable blood/renal tests and normal liver ultrasound. He reported intermittent naproxen for gout and denied alcohol or other hepatotoxins. June 2022 ANA was homogeneous at 1:320 and IgG was elevated at 19.1 g/L; other autoimmune tests were negative and metabolic/HBV/HCV tests were reported normal. FibroScan measured 6.8 kPa with F0–F1 and CAP 187 dB/m.
